records.name: Ignatijs
records.facts_used: Ignatijs: The family leads to Roman Egnatius and later Ignatius. The older name’s meaning is unknown; the spelling was later brought closer to Latin ignis, fire. Fire is therefore a historical association rather than the demonstrated original meaning. The Latvian Language Agency gives the exact rendering Ignatius → Ignatijs, citing page 73 of a 2006 manual. This dated record illustrates transmission between languages; it is not a first birth registration or proof of one borrowing route in every family.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Exact English rendering; Russian Игнатий rendering also exact (1993p199). Unknown Egnatius root retained; reject proven-fire gloss.

records.name: Daujotas
records.facts_used: Daujotas: The Lithuanian guide identifies dau- from daug, much or many, and jot- from jotis, rider. The name preserves the Baltic two-part model. Explaining its stems does not require turning them into one literally translated modern sentence. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Daujotas (Daujys) on 29 November. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Salys PDF318 printed303 November29 visually checked. No first coinage claim.

records.name: Saturninas
records.facts_used: Saturninas: Lithuanian Saturninas corresponds to Latin Saturninus, recorded by Salys. Saturninus is a Roman cognomen formed from the god’s name Saturnus. The original meaning of Saturnus is unknown; the god’s agricultural role is not the literal translation of the name. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Saturninas (Satas, Satys) on 15 December. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: PDF265 printed250 exact Saturninas personal name; PDF318 printed303 December15, not November29. Project calendar unchanged. Guide exact page unavailable, not relied on.

records.name: Egert
records.facts_used: Egert: The Estonian dictionary links the name to a Middle Low German variant of Ekkehard. In this Germanic family ekke denotes a blade’s edge, while hard expresses hardness or strength. The transmission reflects language contact rather than qualities required of every bearer. FIBA’s archive of the 2011 U16 European Championship, Division B, lists Egert Haller for Estonia. Its game list includes Belgium on 28 July. This is a dated sporting example of the exact spelling, rather than the name’s earliest use.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: FIBA exact 2011 event and28July Belgium game; no birthplace, stats or other athlete inferred. Curated Eckhard supplies elements, not an English-surname etymology.
